recipes.name: Roasted Swiss Chard with Feta
ingredients_raw: 1 bunch rainbow chard - leaves and stems separated and chopped
salt and black pepper to taste
4 ounces feta cheese, broken into 1/2 inch pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a baking sheet with olive oil.
Toss chard stems and onions with 1 tablespoon oil in a bowl; season with salt and black pepper. Transfer to the prepared baking sheet.

Bake in the preheated oven until chard stems softened and onion starting to brown on corners, about 15 minutes. Toss chard leaves with remaining 2 tablespoons oil; season with salt and black pepper. Place leaves over stem mixture; scatter feta on top.
Continue baking until stems tender, leaves begin to crisp, and feta melted and golden, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Swiss Chard with Feta
raw_recipe.description: Rainbow Swiss chard is tossed with olive oil and roasted in the oven sprinkled with feta cheese in this hearty side dish.

review.reviewBody:
Stunningly good! The crispy edges on the chard really make this dish. I added a chopped up red bell pepper to the bottom layer and the flavors blended together nicely. I also used fat-free feta. I had to keep myself from eating the entire pan!

Edited to add: I tried this again tonight, using kale instead of chard and goat cheese crumbles instead of feta. Gonna have to give it 5 stars as well. Served it on top of a lemony pasta. So good.

UPDATE: This wonderful dish can be made even better by adding other vegetables to it --- fennel, carrots, red pepper. Add the vegs at the beginning, upping the oven temp to 400º. Reduce to 350º when adding the leaves and feta. This was truly outstanding! It never occurred to me to roast a leafy green vegetable like chard. What a delicious surprise! I followed the recipe except for using a sweet (not yellow) onion. Given the 30-35 minute cooking time, I don't think it really made a difference. The feta worked very well, although I think the chard would be almost as good without it. Will be making this again and often.

We like spicier flavors so I added 3 whole peeled garlic cloves and 2 Serrano peppers quartered lengthwise to the stem mixture. I also cut the roasting time by 1 to 2 minutes on each step to avoid burning.. To make a one dish meal, when the chard was done, I put it in a covered bowl and bumped the oven up to 400 and roasted 1 lb of jumbo shrimp tossed in more olive oil. When done I mixed the shrimp and Swiss chard and had a delicious one pot meal that I will definitely make again. The 4 ounces of feta was the perfect amount, but I did break it up into smaller chunks. I also tossed things at the 1/2 way point of each step (except roasting the shrimp).

OMG! This is incredible! I found a huge (18"x14") chard leaf and discarded the main vein. I used the finger veins but first roasted the onions for 15 min then added those veins for another 5 min then followed recipe. I use a spray avacado oil (higher heat point) instead of evoo so just sprayed the cookie sheet then spray the veggies, add spices and toss a bit. I didn't use salt because of the feta and did top with walnuts. so yummy!!!!

Excellent! Possibly my favorite yet for Swiss Chard. Used sweet Vidalia Onions because it's that time of year. Only used 1 T of oil on the leaves and it was plenty. I love Feta, in part, because a little goes a long way; hence I only used 2 ounces or so. And I forgot to set the timer but I'm guessing I only roasted the leaves for 10 minutes or so and they were nice and crispy; much more and they would have burnt. This was just extra, extra good.

Oh; this is so yummy! I ate it all. Got my green today. :-). The only thing I did different is use lemon pepper, instead of regular pepper. And I cooked it in my air fryer on Roast and just shortened the cooking time. Next time I’m going to add toasted walnuts.

My new favorite way to make and eat chard! I followed the recipe exactly UNTIL it came to cooking method. I cooked it in my new Airfryer (a Christmas gift) as follows: stems & onions cooked at 350 for 8 minutes (might try 10 next time); then leaves & feta for 8 minutes. So quick and delicious! Thank you!

This was a great veggie dish for company as it's so colourful! Don't be wary of the chard stems - they caramelise so nicely, and really give this dish a sweetness and great depth of flavour. I made a few adjustments, making a combination of red chard and green kale and mixed it up with some roasted sweet potato I had on hand (added this later as the cooking time's a bit longer). I also served it up with roasted pine nuts on top. Next time, I'll add a touch of balsamic glaze on top and it really will be 5 stars!

This recipe is very good, picked some fresh swiss chard from my garden and sauté it up (without the stems), some red onion and finished it with some goat cheese, and a touch of Balsamic vinegar. (I didn't have any Feta cheese) It turned out great. Very easy.
Scrumptious! Fresh chard out of the garden, only change I made was of necessity, had no feta so I used an herbed goat cheese and it was incredible. Total keeper

I modified the feta by adding some cream cheese, minced garlic, chives, olive oil, minced sweet onion, and fresh ground black pepper and mixing it all up. I used less olive oil for the chard as well, probably about 1/2 of what the recipe called for. It turned out delicious!!
I used more olive oil and more feta cheese.

Since my husband added Swiss Chard to his enormous garden last year, I have been looking for ways to fix it. I made this tonight and it turned out great! Not sure how much a bunch is, so winged it. I added a little garlic powder to the stems and added fresh basil, rosemary and parsley to the leaves. I'm thinking about adding pine nuts and beets next time. Delicious!

Loved this. It took less time than expected - only 10 minutes after ading chard leaves and feta. I avoid diary, so used vegan feta cheese (Viokase brand). It came in a soft block; I grated it for this recipe. It worked fine. I think I will use less oil next time.
great .. made a lot and it was all gone by end of meal
I added red pepper and garlic. I loved it. My husband, who is extremely picky, said he could eat it again. That is high praise from him for any vegetable dish. I would make this again and enjoy it.
Very tasty and very good for you!!

OMG / this was so good! I almost didn’t make it because I had leftover beef stew to reheat and it didn’t seem compatible but i needed to cook the chard and had crumbled feta and so glad I did! My husband asked why I was making so much - I ate half! Yum!
Simple but great recipe! Next time I'll add lemon zest, and walnuts for a bit of texture.
Always simple, always good.
